question: The 4x4/3-type normalization scan found no inversion, clipping or tie and <=0.51% ratio distortion. Does that bounded-rounding result persist at the generator's default board size 8 (5 ordinary types, 10 pairs) and at board size 6 (4 types, 6 pairs), where integer rounding has more pairs to collapse and large-ratio pairs have lower-valued members?
why_this_is_a_new_question: The published 4x4 report names 'larger type sets' as the main untested boundary of its null result. This test uses a different board geometry and fresh seed block, keeps the published endpoint definitions verbatim, and adds one falsifiable prediction: for every pair, ratio distortion must not exceed 0.5*(1/v_min + 1/v_max) of the two normalized integers, the bound implied by independent integer rounding.

inputs.endpoint_code: .local_agent/profile-normalization-20261018/scan_profile_normalization.py scan_rule() imported directly, so endpoint definitions are identical to the published 4x4 scan

endpoint.primary: Same counts as the 4x4 scan for each board size: rules with an ordering inversion, ceiling clips, floor value 1, tie groups, material tie groups (within-group raw ratio >= 1.10).
endpoint.ratio_distortion: for pairs with raw ratio >= 1.05, |normalized_ratio/raw_ratio - 1|, reported per board size with max and median.
endpoint.quantization_bound: check per pair that distortion <= 0.5*(1/v_min + 1/v_max) + 1e-12; record violations.
endpoint.granularity_relation: report Spearman-free descriptive relation: maximum distortion per rule against that rule's minimum normalized value; state whether the largest distortions sit on the smallest values.
endpoint.promotion_and_hand: same consistency checks as the 4x4 scan.

decision_rule_written_before_run: If any inversion or ceiling clip occurs at either size, record defect_at_larger_size. Else if >=10% of rules at either size carry a material tie, record coarse_normalization_at_larger_size. Else record ratio_rounding_bounded_persists. Record all counts for both sizes either way; do not retune seeds, thresholds or sizes after seeing the result. If the quantization bound is violated for any pair, record bound_violated and report it as a defect in the reasoning, not as a new threshold.
consumer: rule-only generic prices and cross-game ratios: whether the published 4x4 ratio-preservation statement can be extended to the generator's default geometry, or must stay scoped to the toy case.
nonclaims: no search strength or game-outcome claim
no human or external price fit
two board sizes from one generator family and one fresh seed block
a null result at sizes 6 and 8 does not prove ratio preservation for every generated rule
